extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom staff, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: The Society of Professional Journalists' Code of Ethics: principles and actionable standards for gathering, reporting, editing and presenting news across media, intended as a resource for ethical decision-making in newsrooms and classrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code as resource (not rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is voluntarily embraced by thousands of journalists... The code is intended not as a set of 'rules' but as a resource for ethical decision-making. It is not — nor can it be under the First Amendment — legally enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the code to guide decisions rather than as legally binding regulations; consider context and newsroom judgment when applying principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — duty of the journalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should view seeking truth and providing fair, comprehensive accounts as foundational obligations that inform all reporting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy and avoid error
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify claims with multiple sources where possible; correct inadvertent errors promptly; never intentionally alter facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek responses from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact subjects before publication when allegations are involved; document attempts to reach sources; include responses in coverage when received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer named sources; when anonymity is granted, explain why and provide as much contextual information about credibility as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before granting anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether anonymity is necessary for the information to be obtained; set and honor clear terms for confidentiality and document them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all promotional elements accurately reflect story content; avoid sensational or out-of-context extracts that distort meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not distort news photos or video
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted technical edits include color/brightness corrections for clarity; any compositing, montages or illustrative elements must be clearly labeled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading reenactments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present staged or reconstructed scenes as actual footage; clearly identify dramatizations or re-created sequences to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use undercover methods only as last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against deception; disclose to readers/viewers why covert methods were used and what alternatives were tried.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute ideas and text to their original sources; avoid reuse of others' work without clear permission and proper credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse human experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek varied perspectives and voices; resist pressure to avoid controversial but important stories about underrepresented communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and avoid imposing cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on implicit biases; seek cultural context and consult representatives of communities being covered to avoid cultural imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific, factual descriptors rather than generalizations; provide nuance that counters stereotypical portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover a range of opinions fairly; when publishing extreme views, provide context and challenge factual claims where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives from marginalized or less-powerful individuals and communities when relevant to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label opinion, analysis and sponsored content; maintain separation between reporting and advocacy to avoid misleading audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid native advertising that masquerades as news; clearly label paid content and sponsored features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure public business is conducted openly
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue public-records access, FOI requests and transparent reporting on government actions; emphasize accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider emotional impact when interviewing or photographing vulnerable people; adapt approach to minimize additional harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity when using interviews/photos after tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain informed consent, avoid intrusive questioning or imagery, and consider delaying publication when harm may result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge news gathering may cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against potential harm; avoid needlessly intrusive reporting motivated by curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher privacy rights for private people
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between public figures and private individuals; require strong public-interest justification before intruding on privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid lurid pandering
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from sensationalizing details of violence, sex or tragedy purely for audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juveniles/sex-crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect identities of minors and victims where identification could cause harm or violate legal/ethical norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious about naming suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider presumption of innocence and legal implications; avoid premature identification that could damage reputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with legal counsel when necessary; report facts without prejudicing proceedings or influencing jurors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassign coverage or disclose relationships that could undermine impartiality; maintain transparent standards for conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of compromising associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of affiliations that could create biased reporting or perceived partiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse compromising gifts and outside roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish newsroom policies on gifts and outside activities; disclose or decline benefits that create dependence or influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear any relevant financial, personal or professional ties to subjects or organizations covered, both internally and to the audience when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue investigative reporting and oversight of public institutions even in face of pressure; protect sources and reporting integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers/special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep editorial and advertising departments separate; refuse to alter coverage in exchange for revenue or perks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paying for information or bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid practices that create undue influence or unfair access; document payments when unavoidable and disclose to editors/audiences per policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify coverage and invite dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanations of editorial decisions, methodologies and sourcing; offer channels for public feedback and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accessible corrections and complaints processes; treat audience concerns seriously and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue clear corrections and apologies when warranted; correct errors in all platforms where the original appeared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical journalistic practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report on misconduct within the industry; enforce ethical standards through transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by same high standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ethical principles consistently to one's own reporting and conduct as to subjects and institutions being covered.
